description: When task-cli is on PATH (activated and zero-config configured), blocks a raw issue-tracker write that skips its gates: `gh issue`/`linear issue` writes; Forgejo `fj issue create|edit|comment|assign|unassign|close` and `fj repo labels create|delete|edit`; Gitea `tea issues create|close|reopen|edit`, `tea comment`, `tea label create|delete|update`; a REST write (explicit or implied POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE) to `[api/v1|api/v3/]repos/<o>/<r>/issues...` or `.../labels...` via curl, wget, HTTPie or `gh api` on any host (github.com included, for API parity); `gh api graphql` issue/label mutations; and the same REST write from inline Python/Node (`-c`/`-e`, here-string, or an interpreter-fed heredoc), also inside `sh -c`/`bash -c`/`eval`/shell heredocs. An explicit GET/HEAD always wins. Allows `task …`, reads, `--help`, and PR operations. Inert when `task` is not on PATH. A pre-tool guard over the literal command text, not a firewall — README lists the residuals (script files, runtime-built URLs, unlisted interpreters). Fail-closed. No self-service bypass; RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_BLOCK_RAW_TICKET="<justification>" requests one Telegram approval per command (deny-by-default; blank/bare/short values rejected). timeout_ms 960000 covers the hatch helper's 930s worst case; a Claude Code settings entry launching cc_hook_bridge must also set timeout >960s. Installed descriptors execute the primary checkout's source directly, so merging is activation. The block message is a role-aware ladder (agent-tools#994): step 1 is the `task new --title … --acceptance … --why … --impact … --if-not-done …` redo; a subagent is told to `write agent://<parent>` and `yield` awaiting-coordinator (never the human); the coordinator relays and holds the LAST-resort RIG_HATCH_REQUEST_BLOCK_RAW_TICKET line.
